title: Finite-stage etale Verdier biduality
statement:
For every separated finite-type $X/k$, the natural map

$$
\delta_K:K\longrightarrow D_XD_XK
\qquad(K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A))
$$

is an isomorphism. Consequently $D_X$ is an exact contravariant
anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$.

proof.text: For the final specialization use the global finite-stage coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and the small etale categories, not the pro-etale or integral categories. The map is the transpose of evaluation from [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. Keep this coefficient ring fixed, but denote a variable algebraically closed geometric base field by $F$; it is not the global $k$ while the induction is running. Prove the assertion simultaneously over algebraically closed base fields of characteristic different from $\ell$, by strong induction on a dimension bound $d\geq0$: first prove it for proper schemes of dimension at most $d$, then for all separated finite-type schemes of that dimension. The empty scheme has only the zero sheaf and is immediate. Finite-type schemes over a field have finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] and are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. At $d=0$ every point is closed: a proper specialization would give a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length one. Thus the nonclosed-point part of the argument below is vacuous at the base of induction.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 1; supporting Stacks tags: 01T6

proof.text:
First establish preservation independently of biduality, for every algebraically closed field $F$ with $\operatorname{char}F\ne\ell$. Let $X/F$ be separated of finite type with $\dim X\leq d$ and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sf-etale-smooth-stratified-ctf] to obtain the finite localization tower with pieces $Rs_!P$ on smooth strata $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ of pure dimensions $r\leq d$, where $P=s^{-1}K$ has local finite-projective models in $[a,b]$. Factor $s$ as $S\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ with $i$ closed and $j$ open. The ordinary-etale clause of [lem-weil-delta-restriction] gives $j^*\omega_X\cong\omega_V$. The proper composition statement [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition] applies to the closed (hence proper) immersion $i$ and the structure morphism $a_V$ over the actual field $F$. Together with the ambient adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, lem-exc-closed-ambient], it gives, for every ambient complex $C$ on $S$, the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C,Ri^!\omega_V)=\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_*C,\omega_V)=\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{V!}Ri_*C,A)=\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{S!}C,A)=\operatorname{Hom}(C,\omega_S).$$
Yoneda identifies $Ri^!\omega_V$ with $\omega_S$, including counits. Thus $Rs^!\omega_X=Ri^!j^*\omega_X\cong\omega_S$. Apply [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom], whose ordinary-etale clause is unbounded and assumes neither preservation nor biduality, to get
$$D_X(Rs_!P)\cong Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_A(P,Rs^!\omega_X)\cong Rs_*D_SP.$$
All schemes here are separated finite type over $F$, hence Noetherian; no step identifies $F$ with an algebraic closure of a finite field.

proof.text: For the smooth stratum $S/F$ of dimension $r$, [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] gives $\omega_S\cong L[2r]$, with $L$ a locally constant rank-one $A$-sheaf. Its Noetherian base is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, its structure map is smooth separated and compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification], and the coefficient annihilator is invertible in $F$. On an etale cover with the finite-projective model of $P$ and $L\cong A$, internal Hom is the finite dual complex tensored with $L[2r]$: for a finite free module the map $\operatorname{Hom}(A^m,A)\otimes M\to\operatorname{Hom}(A^m,M)$ is the coordinate identity, and projecting this identity by a projective summand's idempotent gives the same identity for a finite projective module. Applying it to each term and to the Hom-complex differential yields $D_SP\cong P^\vee\otimes L[2r]$. The dual terms are finite projective and occupy $[-b,-a]$, hence the shifted complex has Tor interval $[-b-2r,-a-2r]$. Its cohomology is constructible by finite locally constant terms and Serre closure [thm-constructible-serre]. Exact stalks and the tensor-stalk identification [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] with stalk conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] test the local flatness and cohomological bounds, so these bounds hold on $S$. For $s:S\to X$, [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] gives $R^qs_*M=0$ for all module sheaves and $q>2r$. Use the following direct-image calculation, valid over the actual field $F$ and also used in step 10. For any separated finite-type map $f:T\to Y$ between finite-type $F$-schemes with $R^pf_*M=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and $p>N$, and any bounded constructible $G$ of Tor amplitude $[u,v]$, [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] makes $Rf_*G$ bounded constructible. Write $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, a finitely presented $A$-module (one generator and the relation $\varpi_E=0$). The tensor $G\otimes_A^L\kappa_T$ has cohomology only in $[u,v]$ by the Tor hypothesis. Choose its bounded-below representative using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Module sheaf categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck] with terminal index. The convergent finite-filtration spectral sequence [thm-sp-truncation-e2] for $f_*$ has only $0\leq p\leq N$ and $u\leq q\leq v$, so $Rf_*(G\otimes_A^L\kappa_T)$ has cohomology in $[u,v+N]$. The arbitrary-morphism ordinary-etale projection theorem [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] applies: $A$ is Noetherian because it is a finite ring, $G$ is bounded above, and its hypothesis is exactly the displayed all-sheaf bound. It identifies this tensor image with $(Rf_*G)\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y$. The residue criterion [lem-exc-residue-tor-test], which is stated on any scheme with this coefficient ring and bounded constructible input, now gives Tor amplitude $[u,v+N]$ of $Rf_*G$. This derivation invokes no global-base UDV definition. Apply it with $f=s$, $G=D_SP$, $N=2r$, $u=-b-2r$ and $v=-a-2r$. It gives $Rs_*D_SP\in D^b_{ctf}$ with interval $[-b-2r,-a]$, contained in $[-b-2d,-a]$. Apply [lem-sf-hom-triangulated] to each triangle of the finite localization tower of step 2. Starting from its zero end, [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact, thm-constructible-serre] give bounded constructible cohomology of $D_XK$ by induction along the tower. For any degree-zero module sheaf choose a K-flat resolution by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. With this fixed tensor factor, the total tensor and differential of [def-kun-derived-tensor] carry a cone matrix to the cone matrix of the tensored map (including the shift sign); K-flatness makes this operation descend through quasi-isomorphisms. Hence tensoring each triangle gives a distinguished triangle and the same long exact sequence, so the common Tor interval $[-b-2d,-a]$ is preserved by these extensions. This proves $D_XK\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ over every field in the simultaneous induction. Taking $K=A_X$ also proves $\omega_X$ bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude. Preservation here was proved from strata, not from any double-dual isomorphism.

proof.text:
Fix a proper $X/F$ with $\dim X\leq d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$. Set $\Delta=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta_K)$. By the arbitrary-base preservation proved in steps 2--3, both $D_XK$ and $D_XD_XK$ are bounded constructible. The long cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives, for each $q$, an exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal H^q\delta_K)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^q\Delta\longrightarrow\ker(\mathcal H^{q+1}\delta_K)\longrightarrow0.$$
By [thm-constructible-serre] its two end terms and hence its middle term are constructible. Outside a finite interval both end terms vanish. Thus $\Delta$ is bounded constructible; no finite-Tor assertion about the cone is needed.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 3; supporting Stacks tags: 05RS, 03RZ

proof.text: Suppose $d>0$ and $x\in X$ is nonclosed. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$, with finitely many $F$-algebra generators $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ of $B$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], $\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(x)>0$. If every generator had algebraic image in $\kappa(x)$, the fraction field of their image algebra $B/\mathfrak p_x$ would be algebraic over $F$, a contradiction. Choose a generator $t=t_r$ with transcendental image. The coordinate morphism $p:V\to\mathbf A^1_F$ sends $x$ to its generic point, since $F[t]\to\kappa(x)$ is injective. The surjection $F[T_1,\ldots,T_m]\twoheadrightarrow B$ given by the generators gives a closed immersion $V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_F$. Apply [lem-fin-coordinate-generic-dimension] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, $Y=V$ and its open subscheme $V$ itself; $\dim V\leq\dim X\leq d$ follows by viewing chains in an open subspace. Hence $\dim V_\eta\leq d-1$. By [lem-kun-dimension-extension] the same holds for $V_{\bar\eta}$ over $L=\overline{F(t)}$. This fibre is separated and finite type over $L$: on affine charts its rings are obtained from finitely generated $F[t]$-algebras by scalar extension, and its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of $V$; closedness survives scalar extension since $(R/I)\otimes_R R\prime=R\prime/IR\prime$ on affine charts.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 3

proof.text: Write $u:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $g:V_{\bar\eta}\to V$. Verify successively that $u^*K$ and $g^*u^*K$ meet the induction hypothesis's constructibility and Tor conditions. For each of the two pairs $(h,Q)=(u,K)$ and $(g,u^*K)$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies constant-$A$ module pullback $h^*$ with an exact inverse-image functor, so $\mathcal H^q(h^*Q)=h^{-1}\mathcal H^q(Q)$ and the finite cohomological range is preserved. By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback] the pulled-back cohomology sheaves are constructible. On a stratum where a cohomology sheaf is a finite constant $A$-module, pull back its trivializing etale cover and its addition and scalar maps; the result is the same finite constant $A$-module on the pulled-back cover. Thus this is module constructibility, not only constructibility of sets. For a Tor interval $[a,b]$ of $Q$, [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] gives a flat complex $P$ supported in $[a,b]$, representing $Q$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $h^*P$ has flat terms and is K-flat; it is still supported in $[a,b]$. Exactness of $h^*$ identifies its derived object with $h^*Q$, and the converse implication of [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] gives the same Tor interval. Applying these checks first to $(u,K)$ supplies the hypotheses for $(g,u^*K)$. Write $K_V=u^*K$. In particular $g^*K_V\in D^b_{ctf}(V_{\bar\eta,\Et},A)$. All cited pullback statements apply to arbitrary scheme morphisms; the geometric-generic morphism need not be finite type over the original $F$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 4; supporting Stacks tags: 04JC, 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), 0G7E

proof.text:
Work over the variable algebraically closed field $F$ of the induction, and set $L=\overline{F(t)}$ and $T=V_{\bar\eta}$. On the affine $V$ choose generators of its algebra over $F[t]$ to embed $i:V\hookrightarrow W=\mathbf A^r_{\mathbf A^1_F}$ as a closed subscheme. The same immersion after generic base change is $i_L:T\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_L$. By [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition] for the closed immersions, and the Hom-adjunction calculation of step 2,
$$\omega_V\cong Ri^!A_W(r+1)[2r+2],\qquad\omega_T\cong Ri_L^!A_{\mathbf A^r_L}(r)[2r].$$
Apply the closed-support clause of [lem-sf-etale-generic-exchange-algclosed] with $B=\mathbf A^1_F$ and the bounded constructible input $A_W(r+1)[2r+2]$. Tate pullback and invertibility are [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Here is the tensor identity needed for $Ri_L^!$, separately from compatibility of the base-change comparison. Write $h=i_L$, let $Q$ be any invertible locally constant rank-one coefficient sheaf on the ambient affine space, and write $Q_T=h^{-1}Q$. On an etale cover trivializing $Q$, the sheaf direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $h_*(C\otimes Q_T^{-1})=(h_*C)\otimes Q^{-1}$: both sides are the same sections of $C$ on the closed base change of each etale object. These identities agree on overlaps, because multiplication by a transition unit acts identically on both sides. Closed direct image is exact by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], so the identity applies termwise and passes to derived categories. Tensoring with either rank-one sheaf is exact, with its tensor inverse as inverse; on complexes these functors also commute with shifts. The adjunction of [lem-exc-closed-ambient] consequently gives, naturally in $C$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C,Rh^!(M\otimes Q))=\operatorname{Hom}(Rh_*C,M\otimes Q)=\operatorname{Hom}((Rh_*C)\otimes Q^{-1},M)=\operatorname{Hom}(C\otimes Q_T^{-1},Rh^!M)=\operatorname{Hom}(C,(Rh^!M)\otimes Q_T).$$
Yoneda gives $Rh^!(M\otimes Q)\cong(Rh^!M)\otimes Q_T$, compatible with the adjunction counit by construction. Use this with $Q=A(1)$ and the shift $[2]$ to compare the two displayed ambient dualizing objects. Thus there is the canonical comparison $\theta:g^*\omega_V\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_T\otimes J$ with $J=A_T(1)[2]$. Steps 2--3 make $\omega_V$, $K_V$, and $D_VK_V$ bounded constructible, with the last two of finite Tor amplitude, over this actual $F$. Apply the internal-Hom clause of the same new node first to $(K_V,\omega_V)$ and then to $(D_VK_V,\omega_V)$. It identifies $g^*D_VK_V$ with $D_T(g^*K_V)\otimes J$ and $g^*D_VD_VK_V$ with $D_TD_T(g^*K_V)$: in the latter expression $R\mathcal Hom(Q\otimes J,\omega_T\otimes J)=R\mathcal Hom(Q,\omega_T)$, since tensor with the invertible $J$ is an equivalence; this is the Hom adjunction after applying its inverse, and it respects evaluation. The evaluation identity in [lem-sf-etale-generic-exchange-algclosed] says that the two internal-Hom comparisons identify the pulled-back evaluation pairing with evaluation for $g^*K_V$ after the $J^{-1}\otimes J$ cancellation. Transposing that identity via [lem-weil-duality-pairing] therefore identifies the actual arrow $g^*\delta_{K_V}$ with $\delta_{g^*K_V}$, not merely the two underlying objects. The induction hypothesis at dimension $d-1$ over $L$ now makes this arrow an isomorphism. For $u:V\hookrightarrow X$, the ordinary-etale canonical comparison of [lem-weil-delta-restriction] carries $u^*\delta_K$ to $\delta_{K_V}$. Thus the pullback of $\delta_K$ to $T$ is an isomorphism. Given a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ over $x$, use the injection $F(t)\to\kappa(x)\to\Omega$ to choose $L$ inside $\Omega$: take the subfield of elements algebraic over $F(t)$. It is algebraically closed, since a root in $\Omega$ of a polynomial with algebraic coefficients is algebraic over the finite extension generated by those coefficients, and hence over $F(t)$. This is an allowed choice of algebraic closure in the arbitrary-base generic exchange and in the induction hypothesis. Thus $\bar x$ lifts to $V_{\bar\eta}$. Exact inverse image and the stalk comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identify the cohomology stalks of the pulled-back cone with those of $\Delta$ at $\bar x$. They vanish since the pulled-back arrow is an isomorphism. This proves zero stalks at every nonclosed point; exactness of geometric stalks is [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact].

proof.text: For each of the finitely many nonzero $\mathcal H^q\Delta$, its support is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible]; the preceding step shows it consists only of closed points (also at $d=0$). By [def-weil-constructible-subset] it is a finite union of locally closed subsets. Give each such subset its reduced locally closed subscheme structure. It is Noetherian, being a locally closed subspace of the Noetherian $X$, and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Each component has a generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. That point is closed already in $X$, so its closure in the locally closed subscheme is its singleton; hence each component is a singleton. Each support, and then their finite union $Z_0$, is therefore a finite set of closed points. This is the explicit finite-support argument, rather than an assumption that a constructible support is closed.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 4; supporting Stacks tags: 09YS, 005L, 0BA8

proof.text: Record the coefficient identification at $s=\operatorname{Spec}F$. In [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] take $F^{\rm sep}=F$ and the identity geometric point; the Galois group is trivial, so the equivalence is with abelian groups. Transporting the scalar endomorphisms $a\cdot(-)$ for $a\in A$, and their ring identities, gives an equivalence between small-etale constant-$A$ module sheaves on $s$ and $A$-modules. It is exact, since an equivalence of abelian categories preserves kernels and cokernels, and monoidal by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar]. Apply the exact equivalence and its exact quasi-inverse termwise to complexes: they preserve acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms, hence induce inverse derived equivalences. The monoidal equivalence preserves flat objects and K-flat complexes because tensoring with an acyclic complex can be tested through either exact quasi-inverse. Thus the derived equivalence is monoidal; its tensor adjunction identifies derived internal Hom and its evaluation. For the structure map $\operatorname{id}_s$, use the compactification with both maps the identity in [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Extension by zero for the whole open is the identity by its presheaf formula [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]; direct image along the identity is the identity since $W\times_s s=W$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Therefore $R(\operatorname{id}_s)_!$ is the identity. Its right adjoint is the identity as well: the adjunction represents $\operatorname{Hom}(C,-)$ itself, and Yoneda gives the identification with the identity functor. Hence $\omega_s=A_s$. Consequently $D_s$ and its evaluation transpose [lem-weil-duality-pairing] are exactly derived coefficient duality and canonical coefficient evaluation under this equivalence.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 1; supporting Stacks tags: 04JQ, 03QT

proof.text: Let $a:X\to s$ be the proper structure morphism. The ring $A$ is annihilated by a power of $\ell$, invertible in $F$. The all-sheaf vanishing theorem [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] gives $R^ra_*M=0$ for $r>2d$. Apply the arbitrary-base direct-image calculation established in step 3 with $f=a$, $N=2d$, and a Tor interval $[a_0,b_0]$ of $K$; its finite-type, separatedness, invertible-coefficient and bounded-constructibility hypotheses all hold. Thus $Ra_*K$ is bounded constructible with Tor interval $[a_0,b_0+2d]$. Under the point equivalence of step 9 it is a bounded complex of ordinary algebraic $A$-modules with finitely generated cohomology. Indeed constructibility on the one-point scheme gives finite underlying stalk sets, and the elements of each finite set form a finite generating list. Apply [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius] with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $n\geq1$. Its current conventions require commutative coefficients and interpret finite modules as finitely generated, self-injective as injective over the ring itself, and derived Hom on the one-object ringed site. These requirements hold: $A$ is the fixed commutative quotient ring, and step 9 identifies the point category, its tensor, derived internal Hom and evaluation with precisely these ordinary algebraic module constructions. We use its finite-stage clause: $\operatorname{Hom}_A(-,A)$ is exact on modules and evaluation is an isomorphism on finitely generated modules. No ordinary reflexivity assertion for $\mathcal O_E$ is used. For a representing cochain complex $C$, write $(C^\vee)^r=\operatorname{Hom}_A(C^{-r},A)$ with $d_{C^\vee}^r(\phi)=(-1)^{r+1}\phi\circ d_C^{-r-1}$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}_A(-,A)$ makes this dual send acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes, so it computes derived coefficient duality. The transpose of evaluation has degree-$q$ component $c\mapsto(\phi\mapsto(-1)^q\phi(c))$. Substitution in the two displayed differentials verifies that this is a cochain map. Exactness identifies $H^q(C^{\vee\vee})$ with $H^q(C)^{\vee\vee}$; on cocycles the displayed map is finite-module evaluation up to the invertible sign $(-1)^q$. Finite-module reflexivity therefore makes its cohomology an isomorphism for every $q$. Thus its canonical derived coefficient double-dual arrow is an isomorphism, and hence so is $\delta_{Ra_*K}$. Apply [lem-weil-delta-proper-pushforward] to the proper morphism $a$: it identifies this arrow with $Ra_*\delta_K$. Therefore $Ra_*\Delta=0$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] applies to the additive left exact module direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], whose source has enough injectives; it preserves the cone triangle, so the image triangle has an isomorphism as its first arrow. This last cone calculation is independent of geometric biduality.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 05SE, 05SU

proof.text: Put the reduced closed subscheme structure on $Z_0$ and write $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:X\setminus Z_0\hookrightarrow X$. For $M=\mathcal H^q\Delta$, its restriction $j^{-1}M$ has zero geometric stalks by construction of $Z_0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. It is the zero sheaf by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Apply the recollement triangle of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to $M[0]$. Its first term is zero and $i_*$ is exact, so the unit gives $M\cong i_*G$ for the degree-zero sheaf $G=i^{-1}M$. This derives the finite-support representation; the definition of support alone would not give this isomorphism.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 03Q1

proof.text: The reduced finite closed subscheme $Z$ is separated finite type over $F$ with dimension at most zero. The canonical degree-zero formula of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology] says $\Gamma(Z,G)=\prod_{z\in Z_0}G_{\bar z}$. It is $A$-linear because the canonical maps commute with the scalar endomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], these stalks identify with $M_{\bar z}$. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], evaluated at the terminal object, gives $\Gamma(X,M)=\Gamma(Z,G)$. Moreover $\Gamma(Z,-)$ is exact on $A$-module sheaves: its formula is a finite product of exact geometric stalk functors [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and exactness of module sheaves is tested on underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $b=a i:Z\to s$, the point equivalence of step 9 identifies $b_*$ with this exact sections functor, so $Rb_*=b_*$. Since $i_*$ is exact, the ordinary-etale clause of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] gives $Ra_*M=Ra_*i_*G\cong Rb_*G=b_*G$. Thus $R^pa_*M=0$ for $p>0$ and, under the point equivalence, $a_*M=\prod_{z\in Z_0}M_{\bar z}$. This argument works in module sheaves directly and does not silently identify module-derived and abelian-derived cohomology.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5; supporting Stacks tags: 03Q1

proof.text:
Choose $a_0$ below the nonzero cohomology of $\Delta$. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], $\Delta$ has a cochain representative zero below $a_0$; concretely the good truncation has $\operatorname{coker}(d^{a_0-1})$ in degree $a_0$, the original terms above, and zero terms below, and the natural quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism because the discarded cohomology vanishes. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to that bounded-below representative and the left exact additive functor $v=a_*$ on $A$-module sheaves. Both categories of module sheaves are Grothendieck: use [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck] with the terminal index category and a universe in which each small etale site is small. The spectral sequence is therefore
$$E_2^{p,q}=R^pa_*(\mathcal H^q\Delta)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Ra_*\Delta).$$
By step 12 all columns with $p>0$ vanish. The bounded-below hypothesis supplies the theorem's finite, exhaustive, separated filtration in each total degree, so there are no convergence or extension ambiguities: $\mathcal H^q(Ra_*\Delta)\cong a_*\mathcal H^q\Delta$. Step 10 makes the left side zero. The point equivalence and step 12 then give $0=\prod_{z\in Z_0}(\mathcal H^q\Delta)_{\bar z}$. Each factor is zero, by its inclusion and projection in a finite product. Outside $Z_0$ the stalks were already zero. Stalk conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] gives $\mathcal H^q\Delta=0$ for every $q$, whence $\Delta=0$ by the definition of the derived category. Thus $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism for every proper $X$ of dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 5

proof.text: Now let $X/F$ be any separated finite-type scheme with $\dim X\leq d$. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to its structure morphism (the base $s$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated), obtaining a quasi-compact open immersion $j_0:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ with $\bar X$ proper over $F$, as in [def-nagata-compactification]. Replace $\bar X$ by the closed scheme-theoretic closure $C$ of $X$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], the resulting $j:X\hookrightarrow C$ is a quasi-compact dense open immersion. The closed subscheme $C$ remains proper: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $\bar X$, its coordinate rings are quotients of finite-type $F$-algebras, and after every base change the closed immersion remains closed: on affine charts a quotient $R/I$ pulls back to $R\prime/IR\prime$, whose image is the closed subset $V(IR\prime)$. Composing this closed map with the closed map supplied by properness of $\bar X$ proves universal closedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. These verify separatedness, finite type and universal closedness directly. By the dense-open clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension], $\dim C=\dim X\leq d$.

source.place: Q40 agent proof, refining imported Proof paragraph 2; supporting Stacks tags: 01W1

proof.text: Prove the needed preservation by ordinary etale extension by zero directly. For $K$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, use [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] to choose a bounded flat representative $P$ in $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], degreewise $j_!$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and $\mathcal H^q(j_!K)=j_!\mathcal H^qK$, so its cohomological range is unchanged. On each locally closed stratum of a finite constructibility partition of $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] identifies the restricted extended sheaf with the original finite locally constant sheaf; on the complementary closed subscheme it is zero, by that stalk formula and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. The strata are locally closed also in $C$ because $X$ is open. Adding the complement therefore proves constructibility, using the ordinary-etale definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Each term $j_!P^q$ is flat. Indeed, for an injection $M'\to M$ of module sheaves on $C$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives an injection $j^{-1}M'\to j^{-1}M$ on $X$. Tensoring with the flat $P^q$ preserves this injection. At a geometric point of $X$, exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], the extension stalk formula and [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] identify the stalk of $(j_!P^q)\otimes M'\to(j_!P^q)\otimes M$ with the stalk of the just obtained injection $P^q\otimes j^{-1}M'\to P^q\otimes j^{-1}M$. At a point of $C\setminus X$ both stalks are zero. Stalk conservativity proves that $(j_!P^q)\otimes M'\to(j_!P^q)\otimes M$ is an injection, which is the flatness condition. Thus $j_!P$ is a bounded flat complex in $[a,b]$, representing $j_!K$; [lem-pc-kflat-closure] makes it K-flat and the converse implication of [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] gives the same Tor interval. Consequently $j_!K\in D^b_{ctf}(C_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The proper case at the current dimension bound, proved in step 13, gives an isomorphism $\delta_{j_!K}$. Restrict along $j$ and use the ordinary-etale clause of [lem-weil-delta-restriction]: its canonical comparison $(D_X\alpha_{j_!K})^{-1}\circ\alpha_{D_Cj_!K}$ carries $j^*\delta_{j_!K}$ to $\delta_{j^*j_!K}$. Here $j$ is an etale $F$-morphism between separated finite-type schemes, $A$ is finite with invertible additive exponent, and all derived categories have constant $A$-module coefficients, as that clause requires. For an etale object $W\to X$ regarded over $C$, the presheaf formula [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] equals $K(W)$, since $W$ factors through $X$. Sheafification restricted to the open therefore recovers $K$, so $j^*j_!K\cong K$ canonically and this arrow is $\delta_K$. This proves the arbitrary separated finite-type case at dimension bound $d$. At $d=0$ steps 5--7 were vacuous and steps 8--15 prove the base; for $d>0$ the only earlier-dimension use was step 7 over $\overline{F(t)}$. The simultaneous strong induction is therefore well founded.

proof.text: Finally the preservation proved in steps 2--3 makes $D_X$ an endofunctor with reversed arrows on $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$. It is exact contravariantly by [lem-sf-hom-triangulated]. The evaluation transpose is natural by [lem-weil-duality-pairing], and the proved isomorphisms give $\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_XD_X$. Regarding $D_X$ as a functor from the opposite category, its opposite functor is a quasi-inverse: the same natural double-dual isomorphism supplies both composites with the identity. This gives the claimed exact anti-equivalence, with no appeal to an unspecified choice of an isomorphism $K\cong D_XD_XK$. Specialize the proved simultaneous assertion to the original global $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and the fixed coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ to obtain exactly the item statement.
